definition: The ionising radiation that is present around us all the time, mainly from radon gas in the air, rocks and buildings, food and drink, and cosmic rays.
Radiation that can knock electrons out of atoms it passes, turning them into ions; it can damage living cells.
The giving out of radiation by unstable nuclei, which happens by itself, with no outside cause.
The number of counts a detector and counter record per unit time, in counts/s or counts/minute.
The count rate due to a source alone: the measured count rate minus the background count rate, both in the same unit.
